Delusion (Iti 3 3.1)

Conceit (Iti 6 4.1)

Complete Understanding of All (Iti 7 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Complete Understanding of All (Iti 7 2.1)

“Mendicants, without directly knowing and completely understanding the all, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering. By directly knowing and completely understanding the all, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering.”
Complete Understanding of All (Iti 7 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Complete Understanding of All (Iti 7 3.1)

“Those who know the all as all,
are not attracted to anything.
They completely understand all,
and have risen above all suffering.”
Complete Understanding of All (Iti 7 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 2.1)

“Mendicants, without directly knowing and completely understanding conceit, without dispassion for it and giving it up, you can’t end suffering. By directly knowing and completely understanding conceit, having dispassion for it and giving it up, you can end suffering.”
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 3.1)

“These folk are caught up in conceit,
tied by conceit, delighting in existence.
Not completely understanding conceit,
they return in future lives.
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 4.1)

Those who have given up conceit,
freed with the ending of conceit,
vanquishers of the tie of conceit,
have risen above all suffering.”
Complete Understanding of Conceit (Iti 8 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 2.1)

“Mendicants, I do not see a single shroud, shrouded by which people wander and transmigrate for a long time like the shroud of ignorance. Shrouded by ignorance, people wander and transmigrate for a long time.”
The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 3.1)

“There is no other thing
that shrouds people like ignorance.
Veiled by delusion,
they transmigrate day and night.
The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 4.1)

Those who have given up delusion,
shattering the mass of darkness,
wander no more,
the root is not found in them.”
The Shroud of Ignorance (Iti 14 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 2.1)

“Mendicants, I do not see a single fetter, fettered by which people wander and transmigrate for a long time like the fetter of craving. Fettered by craving, people wander and transmigrate for a long time.”
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 3.1)

“Craving is a person’s partner
as they transmigrate on this long journey.
They go from this state to another,
but don’t escape transmigration.
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 4.1)

Knowing this danger,
that craving is the cause of suffering—
rid of craving, free of grasping,
a mendicant would wander mindful.”
The Fetter of Craving (Iti 15 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
A Trainee (1st) (Iti 16 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
A Trainee (1st) (Iti 16 2.1)

“Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very helpful as rational application of mind for a trainee mendicant who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire, but lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke. A mendicant rationally applying the mind gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful.”
A Trainee (1st) (Iti 16 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
A Trainee (1st) (Iti 16 3.1)

“There is nothing so helpful
for a trainee mendicant
aspiring for the ultimate goal
as rational application of mind.
Striving rationally, a mendicant
attains the end of suffering.”
A Trainee (1st) (Iti 16 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
A Trainee (2nd) (Iti 17 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
A Trainee (2nd) (Iti 17 2.1)

“Taking into account exterior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very helpful as good friendship for a trainee mendicant who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire, but lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke. A mendicant who has good friends gives up the unskillful and develops the skillful.”
A Trainee (2nd) (Iti 17 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
A Trainee (2nd) (Iti 17 3.1)

“A mendicant with good friends
is reverential and respectful
when their friends are speaking,
aware and mindful.
Gradually they would attain
the ending of all fetters.”
A Trainee (2nd) (Iti 17 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Schism in the Saṅgha (Iti 18 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Schism in the Saṅgha (Iti 18 2.1)

“One thing, mendicants, arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans. What one thing? Schism in the Saṅgha. When the Saṅgha is split, they argue, insult, block, and forsake each other. This doesn’t inspire confidence in those without it, and it causes some with confidence to change their minds.”
Schism in the Saṅgha (Iti 18 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Schism in the Saṅgha (Iti 18 3.1)

“A schismatic remains for the eon
in a place of loss, in hell.
Taking a stand against the teaching,
favoring factions, they ruin their sanctuary.
After causing schism in a harmonious Saṅgha,
they burn in hell for an eon.”
Schism in the Saṅgha (Iti 18 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Harmony in the Saṅgha (Iti 19 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Harmony in the Saṅgha (Iti 19 2.1)

“One thing, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. What one thing? Harmony in the Saṅgha. When the Saṅgha is in harmony, they don’t argue, insult, block, or forsake each other. This inspires confidence in those without it, and increases confidence in those who have it.”
Harmony in the Saṅgha (Iti 19 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Harmony in the Saṅgha (Iti 19 3.1)

“A Saṅgha in harmony is happy,
as is support for those in harmony.
Taking a stand on the teaching,
favoring harmony, they ruin no sanctuary.
After creating harmony in the Saṅgha,
they rejoice in heaven for an eon.”
Harmony in the Saṅgha (Iti 19 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 2.1)

“Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is corrupted, I understand: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in hell as if delivered there.’ Why is that? Because their mind is corrupted. Corruption of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 3.1)

“Knowing an individual’s
corrupted mind,
the Buddha explained this matter
in the mendicants’ presence.
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 4.1)

If that individual
were to die at this time,
they’d be reborn in hell,
for their mind is corrupted.
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 5.1)

That sort is cast down as surely
as if they’d been carried off and put there.
For corruption of mind is the reason
sentient beings go to a bad place.”
A Corrupted Mind (Iti 20 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 2.1)

“Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is pure, I understand: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in heaven as if delivered there.’ Why is that? Because their mind is pure. Purity of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 3.1)

“Knowing an individual’s
pure mind,
the Buddha explained this matter
in the mendicants’ presence.
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 4.1)

If that individual
were to die at this time,
they’d be reborn in heaven,
for their mind is pure.
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 5.1)

That sort is raised up as surely
as if they’d been carried and put there.
For purity of mind is the reason
sentient beings go to a good place.”
A Pure Mind (Iti 21 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 2.1)

“Mendicants, don’t fear good deeds. For ‘good deeds’ is a term for happiness, for what is likable, desirable, and agreeable. I recall undergoing for a long time the likable, desirable, and agreeable results of good deeds performed over a long time. Having developed a mind of love for seven years, for seven eons of the cosmos contracting and expanding I didn’t return to this world again. As the eon contracted I went to the realm of sublime luminosity. As it expanded I was reborn in an empty mansion of divinity.
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 3.1)

There I was the Divinity, the Great Divinity, the vanquisher, the unvanquished, the universal seer, the wielder of power. I was Sakka, lord of gods, thirty-six times. Many hundreds of times I was a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. My dominion extended to all four sides, I achieved stability in the country, and I possessed the seven treasures. Not to mention regional kingship!
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 4.1)

Then I thought, ‘Of what deed of mine is this the fruit and result, that I am now so mighty and powerful?’ Then I thought, ‘It is the fruit and result of three kinds of deeds: giving, self-control, and restraint.’”
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 4.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 5.1)

“One should practice only good deeds,
whose happy outcome stretches ahead.
Giving and moral conduct,
developing a mind of love:
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 6.1)

having developed these
three things yielding happiness,
that astute one is reborn
in a happy, pleasing world.”
The Benefits of Love (Iti 22 7.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 2.1)

“This one thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, secures equal benefits for both this life and lives to come. What one thing? Diligence in skillful qualities. This is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, secures equal benefits for both this life and lives to come.”
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 2.7)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 3.1)

“The astute praise diligence
in making merit.
Being diligent, an astute person
secures both benefits:
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 4.1)

the benefit in this life,
and in lives to come.
Attentive, comprehending the meaning,
they are said to be astute.”
Both Kinds of Benefit (Iti 23 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 2.1)
“Mendicants, one individual roaming and transmigrating for an eon would amass a heap of bones the size of this Mount Vepulla, if they were gathered together and not lost.”
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 2.2)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 3.1)

“If the bones of a single individual
for a single eon were gathered up,
they’d make a pile the size of a mountain:
so said the great seer.
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 4.1)

And this is declared to be
as big as Mount Vepulla,
higher than the Vulture’s Peak
in the Mountainfold of the Magadhans.
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 5.1)

But then, with right understanding,
one sees the noble truths—
suffering, suffering’s origin,
suffering’s transcendence,
and the noble eightfold path
that leads to the stilling of suffering.
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 6.1)

After roaming on seven times at most,
that individual
makes an end of suffering,
with the ending of all fetters.”
A Heap of Bones (Iti 24 7.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Lying (Iti 25 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Lying (Iti 25 2.1)
“Mendicants, for an individual person who transgresses in one thing, there is no bad deed they would not do, I say. What one thing? It is this: telling a deliberate lie.”
Lying (Iti 25 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Lying (Iti 25 3.1)

“When a personage, spurning the hereafter,
transgresses in just one thing—
lying—
there is no evil they would not do.”
Lying (Iti 25 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Giving (Iti 26 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Giving (Iti 26 2.1)

“Mendicants, if sentient beings only knew, as I do, the fruit of giving and sharing, they would not eat without first giving, and the stain of stinginess would not occupy their minds. They would not eat without sharing even their last mouthful, their last morsel, so long as there was someone to receive it. It is because sentient beings do not know, as I do, the fruit of giving and sharing, that they eat without first giving, and the stain of stinginess occupies their minds.”
Giving (Iti 26 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Giving (Iti 26 3.1)

“If sentient beings only knew
how great is the fruit
of giving and sharing
as taught by the great seer!
Giving (Iti 26 4.1)

Rid of the stain of stinginess,
with clear and confident heart,
they would duly give to the noble ones,
where a gift is very fruitful.
Giving (Iti 26 5.1)

Having given food in abundance
to those worthy of a religious donation,
after passing from the human realm,
the givers go to heaven.
Giving (Iti 26 6.1)

And when they have arrived there in heaven,
they enjoy all the pleasures they desire.
The generous enjoy the
fruit of giving and sharing.”
Giving (Iti 26 7.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 2.1)
“Mendicants, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 3.1)

It’s like how the radiance of all the stars is not worth a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance. Surpassing them, the moon’s radiance shines and glows and dazzles. In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 4.1)

It’s like the last month of the rainy season, in autumn, when the heavens are sunny and cloudless. And as the sun is rising to the firmament, having dispelled all the darkness of space, it shines and glows and dazzles. In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 5.1)

It’s like how, at the crack of dawn, the morning star shines and glows and dazzles. In the same way, of all the grounds for making worldly merit, none are worth a sixteenth part of the heart’s release by love. Surpassing them, the heart’s release by love shines and glows and dazzles.”
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 5.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 6.1)

“A mindful one who develops
limitless love
weakens the fetters,
seeing the ending of attachments.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 7.1)

Loving just one creature with a hateless heart
makes you a good person.
Sympathetic for all creatures,
a noble one creates abundant merit.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 8.1)

The royal potentates conquered this land
and traveled around sponsoring sacrifices—
horse sacrifice, human sacrifice,
the sacrifices of the ‘casting of the yoke-pin’, the ‘royal soma drinking’, and the ‘unimpeded’.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 9.1)

These are not worth a sixteenth part
of the mind developed with love,
as starlight cannot rival the moon.
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 10.1)

Don’t kill or cause others to kill,
don’t conquer or encourage others to conquer,
with love for all living creatures—
you’ll have no enmity for anyone.”
The Meditation on Love (Iti 27 11.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 2.1)

“Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth. What two? Not guarding the sense doors and eating too much. When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.”
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 2.7)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 3.1)

“Eye, ear, nose,
tongue, body, and likewise mind:
a mendicant who leaves these
sense doors unguarded—
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 4.1)

immoderate in eating,
sense faculties unrestrained—
reaps suffering
both physical and mental.
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 5.1)

Burning in body,
burning in mind,
by day or by night
such a person lives in suffering.”
Living in Suffering (Iti 28 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 2.1)

“Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth. What two? Guarding the sense doors and moderation in eating. When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 2.7)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 3.1)

“Eye, ear, nose,
tongue, body, and likewise mind:
a mendicant who makes these
sense doors well guarded—
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 4.1)

eating in moderation,
restrained in the sense faculties—
reaps happiness
both physical and mental.
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 5.1)

Not burning in body,
not burning in mind,
by day or by night
such a person lives in happiness.”
Living in Happiness (Iti 29 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Mortifying (Iti 30 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Mortifying (Iti 30 2.1)

“These two things, mendicants, are mortifying. What two? It’s when someone hasn’t done good and skillful things that keep them safe, but has done bad things, violence and sin. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done good things’, they’re mortified. Thinking, ‘I have done bad things’, they’re mortified. These are the two things that are mortifying.”
Mortifying (Iti 30 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Mortifying (Iti 30 3.1)

“Having done bad things
by way of body,
speech, and mind,
and whatever else is corrupt;
Mortifying (Iti 30 4.1)

not having done good deeds,
and having done many bad,
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
Mortifying (Iti 30 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 2.1)

“These two things, mendicants, are not mortifying. What two? It’s when someone has done good and skillful things that keep them safe, but has not done bad things, violence and sin. Thinking, ‘I have done good things’, they’re not mortified. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done bad things’, they’re not mortified. These are the two things that are not mortifying.”
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 2.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 3.1)

“Having given up bad conduct
by way of body,
speech, and mind,
and whatever else is corrupt;
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 4.1)

not having done bad deeds,
and having done many good,
when their body breaks up, that wise person
is reborn in heaven.”
Not Mortifying (Iti 31 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Ethics (1st) (Iti 32 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Ethics (1st) (Iti 32 2.1)

“Mendicants, an individual with two qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there. What two? Bad conduct and bad view. An individual with these two qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.”
Ethics (1st) (Iti 32 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Ethics (1st) (Iti 32 3.1)

“If a person possesses
these two qualities—
bad conduct
and bad views—
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
Ethics (1st) (Iti 32 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Ethics (2nd) (Iti 33 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Ethics (2nd) (Iti 33 2.1)

“Mendicants, an individual with two qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there. What two? Excellent conduct and excellent view. An individual with these two qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Ethics (2nd) (Iti 33 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Ethics (2nd) (Iti 33 3.1)

“If a person possesses
these two qualities—
excellent conduct
and excellent views—
when their body breaks up, that wise person
is reborn in heaven.”
Ethics (2nd) (Iti 33 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Keen (Iti 34 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Keen (Iti 34 2.1)

“Mendicants, without being keen and prudent a mendicant can’t achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke. But if a mendicant is keen and prudent they can achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.”
Keen (Iti 34 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Keen (Iti 34 3.1)

“Neither keen nor prudent,
lazy, lacking energy,
full of dullness and drowsiness,
unconscientious, lacking regard for others,
such a mendicant is incapable
of experiencing the highest awakening.
Keen (Iti 34 4.1)

One who is mindful, alert, meditative,
keen, prudent, and diligent,
having cut the fetter of birth and old age,
would experience supreme awakening in this very life.”
Keen (Iti 34 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 2.1)

“Mendicants, this spiritual life is not lived for the sake of fawning or flattering people, nor for the benefit of possessions, honor, or popularity, nor thinking, ‘So let people know about me!’ This spiritual life is lived for the sake of restraint and giving up.”
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 3.1)

“The Buddha taught the spiritual life
not because of legends,
but for the sake of restraint and giving up,
and because its objective is extinguishment.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 4.1)

This is the path followed by the great souls,
the great seers.
Those who practice it
as it was taught by the Buddha
doing the Teacher’s bidding,
make an end of suffering.”
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 35 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 2.1)

“Mendicants, this spiritual life is not lived for the sake of fawning or flattering people, nor for the benefit of possessions, honor, or popularity, nor thinking, ‘So let people know about me!’ This spiritual life is lived for the sake of direct knowledge and complete understanding.”
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 3.1)

“The Buddha taught the spiritual life
not because of legends,
but for the sake of insight and understanding,
and because it culminates in extinguishment.
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 4.1)

This is the path followed by the great souls,
the great seers.
Those who practice it
as it was taught by the Buddha
doing the Teacher’s bidding,
make an end of suffering.”
Fawning and Flattery (Iti 36 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Happiness (Iti 37 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Happiness (Iti 37 2.1)

“Mendicants, when a mendicant has two qualities they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements. What two? Being inspired at inspiring places, and making a suitable effort when inspired. When a mendicant possesses these two qualities they’re full of joy and happiness in this very life, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”
Happiness (Iti 37 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Happiness (Iti 37 3.1)

“At inspiring places
an astute person should be inspired;
a keen and alert mendicant
should examine with wisdom.
Happiness (Iti 37 4.1)

A mendicant living like this, with keen energy,
peaceful not restless,
devoted to serenity of heart,
attains the ending of suffering.”
Happiness (Iti 37 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Thoughts (Iti 38 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Thoughts (Iti 38 2.1)

“Two thoughts, mendicants, often occur to the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha: the thought of sanctuary, and that of seclusion. The Realized One loves kindness and delights in it, so this thought often occurs to him: ‘Through this behavior, I shall not hurt any creature firm or frail.’
Thoughts (Iti 38 3.1)
The Realized One loves seclusion and delights in it, so this thought often occurs to him: ‘What is unskillful has been given up.’
Thoughts (Iti 38 4.1)
So, mendicants, you too should love kindness and delight in it, then this thought will often occur to you: ‘Through this behavior, I shall not hurt any creature firm or frail.’
Thoughts (Iti 38 5.1)
You too should love seclusion and delight in it, then this thought will often occur to you: ‘What is unskillful? What is not given up? What should I give up?’”
Thoughts (Iti 38 5.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Thoughts (Iti 38 6.1)

“Two thoughts occur to him,
the Realized One, the bearer of the unbearable:
first mentioned was thought of sanctuary,
then the second made clear was seclusion.
Thoughts (Iti 38 7.1)

Dispeller of darkness, the great seer has crossed over:
the attained, the master, the undefiled.
In the midst of it all, he is freed in the ending of craving;
that sage bears his final body.
He has disposed of Māra, I declare, and gone beyond old age.
Thoughts (Iti 38 8.1)

Standing high on a rocky mountain,
you can see the people all around.
In just the same way, the All-seer, so intelligent,
having ascended the Temple of Truth,
rid of sorrow, looks upon the people
swamped with sorrow, overcome by rebirth and old age.”
Thoughts (Iti 38 9.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Teaching (Iti 39 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Teaching (Iti 39 2.1)

“Mendicants, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha has two approaches to teaching Dhamma. What two? ‘See evil as evil’— this is the first approach to teaching Dhamma. ‘Having seen evil as evil, be disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed from it’— this is the second approach to teaching Dhamma. The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha has these two approaches to teaching Dhamma.”
Teaching (Iti 39 2.8)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Teaching (Iti 39 3.1)

“See the two approaches for
explaining the Dhamma
used by the Realized One, the Buddha,
compassionate for all beings:
Teaching (Iti 39 4.1)

see that that is evil,
and be dispassionate toward it.
Then, with a mind free of desire,
you’ll make an end of suffering.”
Teaching (Iti 39 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Knowledge (Iti 40 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Knowledge (Iti 40 2.1)

“Mendicants, ignorance leads the attainment of unskillful qualities, with lack of conscience and prudence following along. Knowledge leads the attainment of skillful qualities, with conscience and prudence following along.”
Knowledge (Iti 40 2.3)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Knowledge (Iti 40 3.1)

“Bad destinies of whatever kind,
in this world or the next,
are all rooted in ignorance,
compounded of greed and desire.
Knowledge (Iti 40 4.1)

Since one of corrupt wishes is
unconscientious, lacking regard for others,
they brim with much wickedness,
which sends them to a place of loss.
Knowledge (Iti 40 5.1)

Therefore, dispelling desire
and greed and ignorance,
a mendicant arousing knowledge
would abandon all bad destinies.”
Knowledge (Iti 40 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 2.1)

“Those sentient beings are truly bereft, mendicants, who are bereft of noble wisdom. They live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth. Those sentient beings are not bereft who are not bereft of noble wisdom. In this very life they’re happy—free of distress, anguish, and fever— and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 2.7)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 3.1)

“See the world with its gods,
bereft of wisdom,
habituated to name and form,
imagining this is truth.
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 4.1)

Wisdom is best in the world,
as it leads to penetration,
through which one rightly understands
the ending of rebirth and continued existence.
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 5.1)

Gods and humans envy them,
the Buddhas, ever mindful,
of laughing wisdom,
bearing their final body.”
Bereft of Wisdom (Iti 41 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Bright Things (Iti 42 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Bright Things (Iti 42 2.1)

“These two bright things, mendicants, protect the world. What two? Conscience and prudence. If these two bright things did not protect the world, there would be no recognition of the status of mother, aunts, or wives and partners of tutors and respected people. The world would become dissolute, like goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and hounds and jackals. But because the two bright things protect the world, there is recognition of the status of mother, aunts, and wives and partners of tutors and respected people.”
Bright Things (Iti 42 2.7)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Bright Things (Iti 42 3.1)

“Those in whom conscience and prudence
are never found at all,
have lost their bright roots,
and fare on in birth and death.
Bright Things (Iti 42 4.1)

Those in whom conscience and prudence
are always rightly established,
thrive in the spiritual life;
being at peace, they will not be reborn again.”
Bright Things (Iti 42 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 2.1)

“There is, mendicants, freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned. If there were no freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, then you would find no escape here from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned. But since there is freedom from rebirth, freedom from what has been produced, made, and conditioned, an escape is found from rebirth, from what has been produced, made, and conditioned.”
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 3.1)

“What’s reborn, produced, and arisen,
made, conditioned, not lasting,
wrapped in old age and death,
frail, a nest of disease,
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 4.1)

whose inception is the leash to food:
that’s not fit to delight in.
The escape from that is peaceful,
beyond the scope of logic, everlasting,
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 5.1)

where nothing is reborn or arisen,
the sorrowless, stainless state,
the cessation of all painful things,
the blissful stilling of conditions.”
Free of Rebirth (Iti 43 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 2.1)
“There are, mendicants, these two elements of extinguishment. What two? The element of extinguishment with residue, and the element of extinguishment with no residue.
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 3.1)

And what is the element of extinguishment with residue? It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment. Their five sense faculties still remain. So long as their senses have not gone they continue to experience the agreeable and disagreeable, to feel pleasure and pain. The ending of greed, hate, and delusion in them is called the element of extinguishment with residue.
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 4.1)

And what is the element of extinguishment with no residue? It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment. For them, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here. This is called the element of extinguishment with no residue. These are the two elements of extinguishment.”
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 4.6)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 5.1)

“These two elements of extinguishment have been revealed
by the Clear-eyed One, the unattached, the unaffected.
One element pertains to this life—
that with residue though the leash to existence has ended;
and that with no residue, which pertains to what follows this life,
where all states of existence cease.
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 6.1)

Those who have fully understood the unconditioned state—
their minds freed, the leash to existence ended—
attained to the heart of the Dhamma, they delight in ending,
the unaffected ones have given up all states of existence.”
Elements of Extinguishment (Iti 44 7.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Retreat (Iti 45 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Retreat (Iti 45 2.1)

“Enjoy retreat, mendicants, love retreat. Be committed to inner serenity of the heart, don’t neglect absorption, be endowed with discernment, and frequent empty huts. A mendicant who enjoys retreat can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
Retreat (Iti 45 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Retreat (Iti 45 3.1)

“With minds at peace, alert,
mindful and meditative,
they rightly discern the Dhamma,
unconcerned for sensual pleasures.
Retreat (Iti 45 4.1)

Delighting in diligence, peaceful,
seeing fear in negligence,
such a one can’t decline,
and has drawn near to extinguishment.”
Retreat (Iti 45 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 2.1)

“Mendicants, live with training as benefit, with wisdom as overseer, with freedom as core, and with mindfulness as ruler. A mendicant who lives in this way can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 3.1)
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 4.1)

Therefore be always enjoying absorption, immersed in samādhi,
energetic, seers of rebirth’s end.
Having overcome Māra and his armies, mendicants,
go beyond birth and death.”
The Benefits of Training (Iti 46 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Wake Up (Iti 47 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Wake Up (Iti 47 2.1)

“A mendicant should meditate wakeful, mendicants, mindful and aware, joyful and clear, and at times discern the skillful qualities in that state. A mendicant who meditates in this way can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
Wake Up (Iti 47 2.4)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Wake Up (Iti 47 3.1)

“Listen up, wakeful ones!
And those asleep, wake up!
Wakefulness is better than sleep,
the wakeful have nothing to fear.
Wake Up (Iti 47 4.1)

Those who are wakeful, mindful and aware,
immersed in samādhi, joyful and clear,
rightly investigating the Dhamma in good time,
at one, would banish the darkness.
Wake Up (Iti 47 5.1)

That’s why you should apply yourself to wakefulness.
A keen and alert mendicant, possessing absorption,
having cut the fetter of birth and old age,
would experience supreme awakening in this very life.”
Wake Up (Iti 47 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 2.1)

“Mendicants, these two are bound for a place of loss, bound for hell, if they don’t give up this fault. What two? Someone who is unchaste, but claims to be chaste; and someone who makes a groundless accusation of unchastity against a person whose chastity is pure. These are the two who are bound for a place of loss, bound for hell, if they don’t give up this fault.”
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 3.1)

“A liar goes to hell,
as does one who denies what they did.
Both are equal in the hereafter,
those men of base deeds.
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 4.1)

Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth
are unrestrained and wicked.
Being wicked, they are reborn in hell
due to their bad deeds.
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 5.1)

It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained
to eat an iron ball,
scorching, like a burning flame,
than to eat the nation’s alms.”
Bound for Loss (Iti 48 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 2.1)
“Overcome by two misconceptions, mendicants, some gods and humans get stuck, some overreach, while those with vision see.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 3.1)

And how do some get stuck? Gods and humans like clinging, they love it and enjoy it. When the Dhamma is being taught to them for the cessation of existence, their minds do not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided. That is how some get stuck.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 4.1)

And how do some overreach? Some, becoming horrified, repelled, and disgusted with existence, delight in nonexistence: ‘When this self is annihilated and destroyed when the body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death: that is peaceful, that is sublime, that is how it is.’ That is how some overreach.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 5.1)

And how do those with vision see? It’s when a mendicant sees what has come to be as having come to be. Seeing this, they are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be. That is how those with vision see.”
Misconceptions (Iti 49 5.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Misconceptions (Iti 49 6.1)

“Those who see what has come to be as having come to be,
and see the transcendence of what has come to be,
are freed in accord with the truth,
with the ending of craving for continued existence.
Misconceptions (Iti 49 7.1)

They completely understand what has come to be,
rid of craving for rebirth in this or that state.
When what has come to be ceases to be,
a mendicant does not come back to future lives.”
Misconceptions (Iti 49 8.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Roots (Iti 50 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Roots (Iti 50 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three unskillful roots. What three? Greed, hate, and delusion. These are the three unskillful roots.”
Roots (Iti 50 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Roots (Iti 50 3.1)

“When greed, hate, and delusion,
have arisen inside oneself,
they harm a person of wicked heart,
as a bamboo is destroyed by its own fruit.”
Roots (Iti 50 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Elements (Iti 51 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Elements (Iti 51 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three elements. What three? The realm of luminous form, the formless realm, and cessation. These are the three elements.”
Elements (Iti 51 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Elements (Iti 51 3.1)

“Comprehending the realm of luminous form,
not stuck in the formless,
those who are released in cessation,
they are conquerors of death.
Elements (Iti 51 4.1)

Having directly experienced the element free of death,
free of attachments;
having realized relinquishment
of attachments, the undefiled
fully awakened Buddha teaches
the sorrowless, stainless state.”
Elements (Iti 51 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant, painful, and neutral feeling. These are the three feelings.”
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 3.1)

“Stilled, aware,
a mindful disciple of the Buddha
understands feelings,
the cause of feelings,
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 4.1)

where they cease,
and the path that leads to their ending.
With the ending of feelings, a mendicant
is hungerless, quenched.”
Feelings (1st) (Iti 52 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 2.1)

“Mendicants, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant, painful, and neutral feeling. Pleasant feeling should be seen as suffering. Painful feeling should be seen as a dart. Neutral feeling should be seen as impermanent. When a mendicant has seen these three feelings in this way, they’re called a noble mendicant who sees rightly, has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 2.9)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 3.1)

“A mendicant who sees pleasure as pain,
and suffering as a dart,
and that peaceful, neutral feeling
as impermanent
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 4.1)

sees rightly.
And when freed in regards to that,
that peaceful sage, with perfect insight,
has truly slipped their yokes.”
Feelings (2nd) (Iti 53 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for continued existence, and the search for a spiritual path. These are the three searches.”
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 3.1)

“Stilled, aware,
a mindful disciple of the Buddha
understands searches,
the cause of searches,
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 4.1)

where they cease,
and the path that leads to their ending.
With the ending of searches, a mendicant
is hungerless, quenched.”
Searches (1st) (Iti 54 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for continued existence, and the search for a spiritual path. These are the three searches.”
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 3.1)

“The search for sensual pleasures, for continued existence,
and the search for a spiritual path;
the holding tight to the thought, ‘this is the truth’,
and the mass of grounds for views—
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 4.1)

for one detached from all lusts,
freed by the ending of craving,
that searching has been relinquished,
and those grounds for views eradicated.
With the ending of searches, a mendicant
is free of hope and indecision.”
Searches (2nd) (Iti 55 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three defilements. What three? The defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance. These are the three defilements.”
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 3.1)

“Stilled, aware,
a mindful disciple of the Buddha
understands defilements,
the cause of defilements,
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 4.1)

where they cease,
and the path that leads to their ending.
With the ending of defilements, a mendicant
is hungerless, quenched.”
Defilements (1st) (Iti 56 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Defilements (2nd) (Iti 57 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Defilements (2nd) (Iti 57 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three defilements. What three? The defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance. These are the three defilements.”
Defilements (2nd) (Iti 57 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Defilements (2nd) (Iti 57 3.1)

“One who has ended the defilement of sensuality,
whose ignorance has faded away,
and whose desire to be reborn is finished—
liberated, free of attachments,
they bear their final body,
having vanquished Māra with his legions.”
Defilements (2nd) (Iti 57 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Craving (Iti 58 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Craving (Iti 58 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three cravings. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence. These are the three cravings.”
Craving (Iti 58 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Craving (Iti 58 3.1)

“Bound by craving, minds full of desire
for rebirth in this or that state,
yoked by Māra’s yoke, these people
find no sanctuary from the yoke.
Sentient beings continue to transmigrate,
with ongoing birth and death.
Craving (Iti 58 4.1)

Those who have given up craving,
rid of craving for rebirth in this or that state,
they in this world have truly crossed over,
having reached the ending of defilements.”
Craving (Iti 58 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Māra’s Dominion (Iti 59 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Māra’s Dominion (Iti 59 2.1)

“Mendicants, a mendicant with three qualities has slipped free of Māra’s dominion and dazzles like the sun. What three? It’s when they have the entire spectrum of the adept’s ethics, immersion, and wisdom. A mendicant with these three qualities has slipped free of Māra’s dominion and dazzles like the sun.”
Māra’s Dominion (Iti 59 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Māra’s Dominion (Iti 59 3.1)

“Whoever has well developed
ethics, immersion, and wisdom
has slipped free of Māra’s dominion
and dazzles like the sun.”
Māra’s Dominion (Iti 59 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three grounds for making merit. What three? Giving, ethical conduct, and meditation are all grounds for making merit. These are the three grounds for making merit.”
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 3.1)

“One should practice only good deeds,
whose happy outcome stretches ahead.
Giving and moral conduct,
developing a mind of love:
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 4.1)

having developed these
three things yielding happiness,
that astute one is reborn
in a happy, pleasing world.”
Grounds for Making Merit (Iti 60 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
The Eye (Iti 61 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
The Eye (Iti 61 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three eyes. What three? The eye of the flesh, the eye of clairvoyance, and the eye of wisdom. These are the three eyes.”
The Eye (Iti 61 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
The Eye (Iti 61 3.1)

“The eye of flesh, the clairvoyant eye,
the supreme eye of wisdom:
these three eyes
were taught by the supreme person.
The Eye (Iti 61 4.1)

The arising of the eye of flesh
is the path to the clairvoyant eye.
When knowledge arises—
the supreme eye of wisdom—
one who gains that eye
is released from all suffering.”
The Eye (Iti 61 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Faculties (Iti 62 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Faculties (Iti 62 2.1)

“Mendicants, there are these three faculties. What three? The faculty of understanding that enlightenment is imminent. The faculty of enlightenment. The faculty of one who is enlightened. These are the three faculties.”
Faculties (Iti 62 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Faculties (Iti 62 3.1)

“As a trainee trains,
following the straight road,
first they know about ending;
enlightenment follows without delay.
Faculties (Iti 62 4.1)

Then the knowledge comes
to such a one, freed through enlightenment,
with the end of the fetters of continued existence:
‘My freedom is unshakable.’
Faculties (Iti 62 5.1)

Accomplished in the faculties,
peaceful, in love with the state of peace,
they bear their final body,
having vanquished Māra with his legions.”
Faculties (Iti 62 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Periods (Iti 63 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Periods (Iti 63 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three periods. What three? Past, future, and present. These are the three periods.”
Periods (Iti 63 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Periods (Iti 63 3.1)

“Sentient beings who perceive the communicable,
become established in the communicable.
Not understanding the communicable,
they fall under the yoke of Death.
Periods (Iti 63 4.1)

But having fully understood the communicable,
they don’t conceive a communicator,
as they’ve touched liberation with their mind,
the supreme state of peace.
Periods (Iti 63 5.1)

Accomplished in the communicable,
peaceful, in love with the state of peace;
one who makes use after appraisal, firm in principle,
a knowledge master cannot be reckoned.”
Periods (Iti 63 6.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of bad conduct. What three? Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. These are the three kinds of bad conduct.”
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 3.1)

“Having done bad things
by way of body,
speech, and mind,
and whatever else is corrupt;
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 4.1)

not having done good deeds,
and having done many bad,
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
Bad Conduct (Iti 64 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Good Conduct (Iti 65 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Good Conduct (Iti 65 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these kinds of good conduct. What three? Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. These are the three kinds of good conduct.”
Good Conduct (Iti 65 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Good Conduct (Iti 65 3.1)

“Having given up bad conduct
by way of body,
speech, and mind,
and whatever else is corrupt;
Good Conduct (Iti 65 4.1)

not having done bad deeds,
and having done many good,
when their body breaks up, that wise person
is reborn in heaven.”
Good Conduct (Iti 65 5.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Purity (Iti 66 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Purity (Iti 66 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of purity. What three? Purity of body, speech, and mind. These are the three kinds of purity.”
Purity (Iti 66 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Purity (Iti 66 3.1)

“Purity of body, purity of speech,
and undefiled purity of heart.
A pure one, blessed with purity,
has given up everything, they say.”
Purity (Iti 66 4.1)
This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
Sagacity (Iti 67 1.1)
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
Sagacity (Iti 67 2.1)
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of sagacity. What three? Sagacity of body, speech, and mind. These are the three kinds of sagacity.”
Sagacity (Iti 67 2.5)
The Buddha spoke this matter. On this it is said:
Sagacity (Iti 67 3.1)

“A sage in body, a sage in speech,
a sage undefiled in mind;
a sage, blessed with sagacity,
has washed off all bad things, they say.”
